item.title: China bids to host secretariat of new high seas treaty days after Trump withdraws US from 66 global orgs
item.description: China on Friday proposed to host the secretariat of a new treaty governing the high seas, a surprise bid that underscores Beijing’s desire to have greater influence over global environmental governance. item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Hong Kong’s dwindling LGBTQ funding scheme mainly goes to groups with no ties to community
item.description: Five of the seven groups awarded funding under a government scheme for projects on sexual minorities have no track record of LGBTQ-related work, prompting concern among veteran activists about their effectiveness. The recipients include groups that organise beach clean-ups and artificial intelligence (AI) classes. Most have apparent pro-establishment ties, an HKFP investigation has found. They […]

item.description: By Lydia Catedral & MICROLAB At 4.34pm on November 26, Sringatin and Jepy saw a WhatsApp message from a relative of an Indonesian domestic worker who was trapped inside a burning building in Wang Fuk Court, a housing estate in Tai Po. item.title: China tells Cambodia scam hub disappearances threaten ties
item.description: China’s embassy in Cambodia said on Saturday that a recent spate of disappearances of Chinese nationals into cyberfraud compounds poses a “serious obstacle” to the allies’ ties. Ambassador Wang Wenbin urged Phnom Penh to strengthen a crackdown on the illicit industry in a meeting with Cambodia’s top ministers, a statement on the embassy’s WeChat account […]

item.title: US lawmakers call for Hong Kong trade offices to be closed, as Beijing ministry slams ‘political grandstanding’
item.description: China’s foreign ministry in Hong Kong has condemned US lawmakers’ calls for Washington to strip the city’s trade offices of their privileges, slamming the move as evidence of “deep-seated ideological bias.” The Commissioner’s Office of the Foreign Ministry in Hong Kong’s comments in a Saturday statement came days after US bipartisan lawmakers reintroduced a bill […]

item.title: Police drones to be deployed around The Peak, Lamma Island and Cheung Chau as pilot scheme enters 2nd phase
item.description: Hong Kong police will expand the use of drones for crime prevention to areas including The Peak, Cheung Chau and Lamma Island as part of a pilot scheme. item.title: China’s 2025 economic growth among slowest in decades
item.description: China’s economy grew at one of the slowest rates in decades last year, according to official data released Monday, as officials struggle to overcome persistently low consumer spending and a debt crisis in the country’s property sector. item.title: Two more college student unions at Chinese University of Hong Kong cease operations
item.description: Two more college student unions at the Chinese University of Hong Kong’s have ceased operations, leaving behind only two other registered student unions representing colleges at the university. item.title: China’s birth rate falls to lowest on record despite nationwide policies to curb decline
item.description: China’s birth rate plunged last year to its lowest level on record, official data showed on Monday, as its population shrank for a fourth straight year despite efforts to curb the decline. item.title: Colleagues of firefighter who died in Tai Po blaze run half-marathon in his honour
item.description: Colleagues of Ho Wai-ho, the firefighter who died in the Tai Po blaze, ran a half marathon in his honour at Sunday’s Standard Chartered Hong Kong Marathon event.
